text:
Iris: Noticing a tight spike in P95 and several fractional-dedicated evictions from us-west-2 rack-3 starting 18:12 UTC. Short chat latency up ~90ms.
Tom: Any NVLINK/PCIe signs?
Iris: nvlink tx bursts and PCIe write stalls coincide with NIC tx spikes. Pattern looks like host-local IO flare.
Velma: Could be a large ad-hoc data prep job landing on those hosts. Can we throttle best-effort cgroup briefly?
Raghu: Quick mitigation: deploy eBPF pacer to the affected hosts and set allocator to avoid rack-3 for 15m. I can do both.
Iris: do it. Add a requeue cooldown of 75s so tenants don't bounce back fast.
Raghu: Commands I'm running:
```
fleetctl run --hosts rack-3 "ebpf-pacer --cgroup best-effort --egress 45% --tag incident-3234567000"
kubectl patch cm allocator-policy -n fleet -p '{"data":{"avoid_rack_3":"true","requeue_cooldown_s":"75"}}'
```
ops-bot: eBPF pacer job scheduled on 4 hosts in rack-3. Allocator patch applied.
Tom: Can you add a small panel for "nvlink_tx_burst" next to preemptions and requeue_same_rack_count?
Velma: I'll add it and set a temporary alert nvlink>80% for 90s. Mute for 2m while we deploy to avoid noise.
Raghu: applied pacer, nvlink_tx_burst down ~28% in 70s, preemptions dropping. requeue_same_rack_count down ~42% after 10m.
Iris: partial win. Keep pacer for 20m and then evaluate. Long-term we should consider host IO QoS + allocator bias away from recent nvlink spikes.
Tom: agree. Open a ticket for allocator heuristic work and notebook historical analysis of nvlink-driven regressions.
Velma: created INF-9001 (allocator nvlink-avoid heuristic) and INF-9002 (host IO QoS runbook).
Iris: thanks. I'll update the incident board once we hit the 20m mark. :white_check_mark:
